snapshot.scope: Current development build and existing scoped evidence. Re-audit classifications after source, output, release or platform evidence changes.

status_definitions.verified: Full applicable shipping contract including behavior, visuals except Settings allowance, safety, inputs and accessibility, tested against release on macOS, Windows and Linux and linked to exact candidate identities. No exception assumed.
status_definitions.partial: Some specific capability has evidence but at least one shipping or cross-platform condition remains open.
status_definitions.known_gap: At least one specified requirement is confirmed unimplemented or available only as an isolated draft.
status_definitions.unassessed: No sufficiently current assessment here; not evidence of absence or completeness.

items.name: Island chrome (pill + command bar)
items.shipping_contract: Resting pill shows back/forward (desktop; mobile uses edge-swipe per D7), standalone-pin + active-section dots (cap 8 + window-wide `+N`; pointer platforms reveal a dot's favicon on hover/focus), favicon, domain, shield count (clickable → site-protection popover on desktop), private chip, action cluster. Expanded states: panel / palette / find. Desktop has opt-in 300 ms hover-open and an opt-in auto-hiding strip; touch-only mobile has no hover equivalent.
items.reason: Missed Shield close clicks reproduced; paired native hit-region fix remains unbuilt. Reconciled assets pass simulated-capability geometry and injected rejection/retry checks in isolated fixtures; actual fixed-native interaction, page pass-through, drag, accessibility and other platforms remain open.

items.name: Tabs (create/close/switch/reopen/duplicate/pin/mute)
items.shipping_contract: Same lifecycle + same reopen-closed and pin/mute semantics. Desktop recovery is scoped to the native workspace that closed the tab (D11). Pins remain in their current group and lead it; ungrouped pins use a standalone shelf. Plain new tab is always ungrouped. An inactive tab may have its renderer discarded and rebuilt (D8, F31) without losing identity, title, address, or back-history.
items.reason: Combined Mac candidate now disables Close Above/Below when no unpinned tabs are on that side; scripted regular/private checks confirm state and preservation of pinned/selected tabs. Tab selection and two-pane identity have focused checks. Full lifecycle, interactions and platform parity remain open; candidate is unpromoted.

items.name: Tab groups
items.shipping_contract: Names (with an optional Spaces preset color), kept in the case typed and matched in any case; renamable from the header. Group exists only while non-empty. Pill renders standalone pins + the active section and counts every omitted tab in `+N`. Same create/move/ungroup/close-group actions. iOS (M17, unreleased): groups as tab-grid sections and in the palette, synced with shared Spaces; dragging into groups comes later.
items.reason: Isolated Chromium 158 candidate has scoped native group creation, rename and activation checks on Mac; complete group actions, current development promotion, shipping comparison, accessibility and other platforms remain open. The previously verified 158 native group handler is now retained in repository source; 157 compilation and preparation of the matching newer Start Page assets remain open.

items.name: Private tabs
items.shipping_contract: Never in history/session/reopen; inherited by child tabs; isolated non-persistent web session; private theme + quick-exit chip. M9 iOS client implemented, unreleased: `/private`, one in-memory web session shared by private tabs and forgotten when the last one closes, page-opened children stay private, never saved, synced or in History, private theme and a Private chip that closes the tab.
items.reason: Focused primary-incognito Start Page checks exist; the entire private-tab contract remains unproved.

items.name: Address input & search
items.shipping_contract: Same normalization heuristic + engine choice (DuckDuckGo/Google/Bing/Brave/Kagi, or a custom address). Best-effort autocomplete follows the current default; opt-out, private tabs, pasted/dropped text, local paths, URL-like input, and credential-like prefixes stay local. OS hand-off for `mailto:`/`tel:`/etc.; desktop additionally confirms reviewed app/OAuth callback schemes.
items.reason: Live search still hardcodes Google. The selected-provider candidate built with a zero-action guard. Synthetic regular and private native and Island searches reached loopback; the private Island closed after commit and a separate closed-database readback found no private markers. The fixture itself failed its original SQLite read. Independent host-wide isolation, stock providers, real privacy and fresh-profile defaults remain open. A fresh-default draft is unintegrated: global fallback replacement could change existing users and native choice-screen eligibility.

items.reason: Isolated Chromium 158 regular/private scripted tab and group matching passed; regular Favorite/history ranking, deduplication and selection passed. Seeded private check confirms Chromium hides regular Favorites and History, whereas released shipping source lists them; privacy-preserving parity remains unresolved. Native keyboard, accessibility, visual parity and Windows/Linux remain open.

Send to device remains M7b. M17 (unreleased): the iOS snapshot publishes its groups and, with Spaces sync on, a `shared` sidecar; tabs another device binds to a shared Space the phone holds are listed once.

items.name: Quiet Tabs (idle renderer discard)

Restored sessions come back quiet. The state is called "quiet" in every user-visible and assistive string.

items.name: Glance reference pane
items.shipping_contract: A desktop window can show one explicitly chosen local tab as a temporary reference; dismissal leaves the tab open, and ownership never crosses a window or profile. Unreleased on main since v1.39.0: the reference is a movable, resizable card floating over the page (Open as tab replaces Make main's swap; a tab switch closes it). iOS offers it at regular width only (D30).
items.reason: Native temporary pair/conversion exists. Staged native geometry matches released floating-card arithmetic in 4,200 finite cases; an unbuilt floating view and live-state implementation and an unrun isolated browser harness are prepared. Its private card palette switches in a mocked-surface check; mixed-profile theme behavior remains unimplemented. Staged Keep as Split uses the native pivot transaction instead of separate regrouping; grouped conversion remains unrun and pinned pairs remain refused. The released model pins the pair when either tab is pinned, and preserves the main group and newly pinned homes; Chromium pivot pinning and post-conversion grouping differ. Actual browser behavior, foreground/background page visibility, focus, security, accessibility and desktop-platform parity remain unverified.

items.name: What's New page
items.shipping_contract: Desktop only. Opens blanc.day's page for a feature release once after the update, only when the page exists; the Start Page pill links to it.
items.reason: No full three-platform parity assessment recorded in this tracker.

items.name: Tab Archive
items.shipping_contract: Desktop only. Off by default, device-local. Idle ungrouped, unpinned tabs close into a per-profile Archive kept 30 days, restorable from the Quick Switcher and History; never private tabs, never synced, cleared with history.
items.reason: No full three-platform parity assessment recorded in this tracker.

items.name: Split View
items.shipping_contract: Desktop, and iOS regular width (two panes, D30). Two to four tabs side by side, one row in the tab list, saved with the session and Spaces; grown out of Glance; one Island plus a header per pane.
items.reason: The new unpromoted Mac candidate passes isolated regular/private menu pin and unpin for both panes while preserving split and pane order. The running development app remains older; pinned-home/group handling, veto/races, physical input, four-pane layouts, visual/accessibility and Windows/Linux remain open.

items.name: Billboard clock Font & color
items.shipping_contract: Desktop only. Four bundled faces (Roboto Flex added) with weight and a type-designed height from each face's width axis, Automatic or a Spaces preset at a tone, Solid or a refracting Glass, and a shadow that keeps it readable on any background; synced; values finished in a pure module.
items.reason: Start Page clock controls have scoped candidate checks; complete shipping sync, visual/accessibility and all-platform acceptance remain open.

items.name: Reader Mode
items.shipping_contract: Free manual local article reading, shared sanitizer/reading UI and appearance defaults, source identity and return without reload; no reader-content persistence or sync. Candidate only; platform release gates pending. iOS reuses already-loaded canvas-readable images.
items.reason: No integrated Reader capability. Shipping extraction and presentation pass isolated fixtures; native guard passes fake-interface checks, and image format/accounting drafts pass standalone checks. Real browser authority, companion, blocker-safe image broker, UI and desktop platforms remain open.

items.name: Switch tabs in the order you used them
items.shipping_contract: Desktop only. Ctrl+Tab steps back through tabs by most recent use and lands when Ctrl is released; Esc cancels; Ctrl+PageDown/PageUp keep list order. A favicon-strip card from the second step; click to land, Ctrl+W closes the pick. Linux only until the Ctrl release is proven on Windows and macOS.
items.reason: Shipping v1.45.1 supports a held-key recent-tab session on Linux/Windows; Chromium native MRU immediately activates one prior tab. An unintegrated shipping-model adapter and card pass seven unit tests and an isolated headless DOM composition check; native input, actual tab activation, full UI and platform behavior remain open.

items.name: Open links from other apps where they belong
items.shipping_contract: Desktop only. Ordered domain/contains rules in Settings → Profiles send links other apps hand Blanc to a profile, optionally a Space (opened in a new window when not showing) and a private tab; unmatched links keep the window used last. Device-local, never synced. The shield popover's switch and `/route [off]` make a rule for the site in view. Opt-in: links the person opens in a new tab from a page follow rules that point elsewhere (never popups, private tabs or same-tab clicks). Candidate only.
items.reason: No full three-platform parity assessment recorded. v1.45.1 requires a background-routed new window to preserve focus in the originating window; foreground routes still activate normally. No routing implementation was found in the primary prototype bridge during this limited check; broader audit remains open.

items.name: Launch Sunrise on startup
items.shipping_contract: See referenced v1.45 release notes and actual shipping implementation; possible exceptions are not automatically waived.

Development qualification and full persistence, accessibility and cross-platform parity remain open.
